title: marketplace-integrator-quickstart-copy-and-compliance-checklist
content:
Purpose

Quick internal draft: compact playbook for partner integrators who will publish a Redwood image in cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). Focus is two things: 1) a tight set of copy variations that partner ops can drop into listing forms, and 2) an operational preflight & compliance checklist to avoid late blockers (billing, trial entitlements, data residency, KMS, security reviews).

Context / why this exists
- We have repeated last-minute asks from partners and marketplaces during publication (missing trial copy, SSO details, SKU mismatch). This doc consolidates the most frequent gaps into copy snippets + a short acceptance checklist.
- Intended audience: partner ops, partner engineers, listing authors, and PMs running marketplace publishing sprints.

High-level TL;DR (for quick cut-and-paste)
- Short product tile (<= 80 chars): "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference, hosted or private"
- One-liner summary (<= 200 chars): "High-performance LLM inference with predictable latency and costs. Choose hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, or VPC/private deployment for regulated data."
- Trial CTA (one sentence): "Start a 14-day trial — no credit card required; includes 100k free tokens and guided onboarding."

Listing metadata guidance
- Suggested categories: AI & ML, Dev Tools, Databases & Storage (if private), Security & Compliance (if Private offering)
- Keywords/tags: inference, llm, gpu, low-latency, private-deployment, dedicated-gpu, VPC, embeddings, model-serving
- Contact: solutions@redwood.ai (replace with partner-specific alias when co-branded)

Copy variants (short, medium, long)
- Tile (short, 60–80 chars):
  "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference for production apps"

- Short description (<= 200 chars):
  "Run LLMs in production with predictable latency and transparent unit economics. Hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, or private VPC deployments with enterprise SLAs and audit logs."

- Medium description (200–500 chars):
  "Redwood Inference provides a production-first LLM serving platform that balances latency, cost, and reliability. Ship features quickly with our hosted API, reserve Dedicated GPU capacity for predictable throughput, or deploy Private instances in your VPC for regulated workloads. Built-in telemetry, rollouts, and cost-optimization tooling help you stay performant and efficient."

- Long description (500–1000 chars):
  "Redwood combines a high-throughput serving runtime with orchestration and observability designed for production LLM workloads. Optimize latency and cost with intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and model/quantization recommendations. Choose hosted for fast onboarding, Dedicated reserved pools for throughput guarantees, or Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency and compliance. The Console provides per-route traces, token-level cost analytics, and rollout controls (canary, A/B, automatic fallback). Enterprise integrations: SSO (SAML/OIDC), KMS/HSM, audit logging, and SOC/ISO compliance packages. Quickstarts, SDKs, and partner integrations available."

Features bullets (for listing feature section)
- Production-grade latency and throughput controls
- Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes
- Per-route cost and latency analytics, tracing hooks
- Canary/A-B/automatic fallback rollouts
- Built-in KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs
- Embeddings, chat, reranking, streaming responses

CTA / trial language variants (choose one depending on marketplace rules)
- Variant A (recommended): "Start 14-day trial — includes 100k free tokens and guided onboarding. No credit card required."
- Variant B (if marketplace forbids "no credit card required"): "Start 14-day trial. Guided onboarding included; billing will begin after trial unless canceled."
- Variant C (enterprise/SSO flows): "Request a dedicated trial and on-boarding for Dedicated/Private deployments. Contact solutions@redwood.ai."

Pricing & SKU mapping guidance (short checklist)
- Single SKU for hosted API with usage-based pricing (per token); additional SKU(s) for Dedicated (monthly reserved commit) and Private (custom license).
- Marketplace listing should not publish per-token price in copy; use ranges or starting price (e.g., "starting from $0.XX per 1k tokens for hosted API") only if allowed by marketplace pricing rules.
- Trials must be mapped to trial entitlement SKUs in partner console (important: mismatch caused GTM delay for 3 partners in last quarter).

Compliance and legal flags (do not forget)
- Data residency note for EU customers: "Data processed in EU regions only — contact us for region lock" (only show if customer opts in and Dedicated/Private available).
- KMS and key control: provide clear copy that KMS is available for Private and Dedicated; for hosted API note that we support customer-managed keys via partner provisioning when available.
- Privacy/data use: default copy must include: "Redwood does not retain customer prompt data beyond inference caching used to optimize latency unless otherwise contracted." (Legal: check with privacy@redwood.ai before final)
- Security badge copy (SOC2/SOC3/ISO): only include after legal verification and asset availability. Do not assert compliance that we do not have.

Preflight acceptance checklist (operational gate)
- Listing metadata completed (title, descriptions, tile image, logos in specified dimensions)
- Trial SKU mapping verified in marketplace console (JIRA ticket for entitlement mapping if not)
- Pricing SKUs (hosted/dedicated/private) created and tested in sandbox purchase flow
- Legal copy signed off (privacy, billing terms, data residency) — attach legal ticket or Confluence page
- Security review complete: attach security approval artifact or sec-app ticket (must include KMS handling if advertised)
- Integration QA: verify SSO redirect URIs, provisioning flow, and any IAM roles (for private connectors)
- Demo/test account configured and link provided (with sample tokens and limited capacity)

Marketplace-specific notes (common gotchas)
- AWS: ensure AMI/stack listing includes a valid support contact and versioning info. Confirm AWS marketplace trial entitlement mapping (often manual).
- Azure: publisher requires specific legal wording for trial cancellation and billing start; double-check with partner ops.
- GCP: verify pricing tiers and metered billing mapping; watch quotas for first week of listing.

Telemetry & events to instrument on listing flows (so we can measure conversions)
- listing_view (tags: tile_id, partner_id, region)
- trial_started (tags: tile_id, partner_id, trial_type)
- trial_activation_complete (user_id, cluster_type)
- purchase_commit (sku_id, commit_type)
- onboarding_session_started (session_id, partner_rep)

Localization and copy hygiene
- EU localized copy should avoid phrases like "no credit card required" if region rules differ — use neutral phrasing and confirm with legal.
- Keep short tile <80 chars; some marketplaces truncate at 60 on mobile. Provide both 60- and 80-char options.
- Avoid marketing superlatives that may trigger marketplace review ("best", "fastest"). Use factual claims and metrics where available (e.g., "<50ms median latency on typical 2k token workload"), but check with bench-marking team for numbers.

Design assets (quick notes)
- Tile art: 1200x628 (landscape), include clear logo, short tagline. Provide both light and dark background versions.
- Screenshots: Console dashboard, per-route analytics, and rollout UI. Blur any customer PII.

Smoke-test script (copy for partner QA)
1) Open listing in sandbox and confirm tile shows short tile and short description
2) Click trial CTA and verify trial entitlement appears in partner console and redirects to onboarding flow
3) Run a simple generate call against trial credentials: generate("Hello world") -> verify response, latency within expected bounds, and tokens consumed reflected in dashboard
4) Verify billing screenshot appears in sandbox purchase flow (if applicable)
5) Confirm SSO login flow (SAML/OIDC) for private/dedicated trials

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Q: Can marketing share official throughput/latency numbers for the long description? Need benchmark owner to confirm numbers. (Assigned: Ethan)
- Q: Does partner want "no credit card required" on trial CTA for APAC markets? Legal/regulatory differences may apply. (Assigned: Marina)
- TODO: create lightweight checklist card in partner-portal with the acceptance checklist above. (Owner: Priya)
- TODO: Add step-by-step SKU mapping doc for AWS/Azure/GCP with screenshots (follow-up GH PR).

Change log / history
- 2025-01-18 — initial draft created by Priya Sharma
- 2025-01-24 — added telemetry event names and trial CTA variations (Ethan Lin)
- 2025-02-02 — updated compliance flags and QA script (Marina Kovács)

Quick copy bank (snippets for easy copy-paste)
- Short tile: "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference for production apps"
- Short line: "Predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, Dedicated, Private)."
- Trial CTA A: "Start 14-day trial — includes 100k free tokens and guided onboarding. No credit card required."
- Trial CTA B: "Start 14-day trial. Billing begins only after trial unless canceled."

End notes
- This is deliberately compact — will expand to marketplace-specific subpages once we confirm pricing SKUs and legal signoffs.
- Please leave inline comments in the Confluence page (link above) or ping #partner-marketplace on Slack for urgent review.
